title: Leaked LiteLLM Master Key Let Attackers Steal GitHub Tokens and Hijack Release Pipeline
summary: An accidentally leaked password allowed hackers to take over the LiteLLM project's release system and push malicious software. This compromised package could steal sensitive login information and computer secrets from users.

also_covered.title: LiteLLM release pipeline hacked to distribute info-stealer malware

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you or your workplace use LiteLLM Python packages or Docker images, check with your IT team immediately to ensure you are not running the compromised versions.
action_it: Audit environments for affected LiteLLM Python packages and Docker images. Revoke and rotate any compromised credentials, GitHub tokens, and environment variables associated with the deployment.

title: CISA Flags Two Actively Exploited Critical Flaws in Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud
summary: U.S. cybersecurity authorities added two critical software flaws to a catalog of actively exploited vulnerabilities. Organizations using the affected software need to take immediate protective measures.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses these enterprise systems, your IT team should handle the updates.
action_it: Review CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog for these entries and apply the necessary vendor patches immediately.

title: Ruby Fixes Three Regex Engine Bugs Responsible for Four Critical GitLab RCE Flaws
summary: Ruby released updates to fix three bugs in its built-in regular expression engine. These bugs allowed four critical security flaws that GitLab recently patched to potentially let attackers run unauthorized code on servers.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses GitLab or Ruby, your IT team should already be aware of these updates.
action_it: Apply the latest Ruby security releases (versions 4.0.9, 3.4.12, and 3.3.13) and ensure all related GitLab patches are fully applied.

title: HPE patches eight max severity RCE and auth bypass AOS flaws
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise released security updates to fix 72 vulnerabilities in its Aruba network software, including eight maximum-severity flaws that could let hackers take control of systems. These flaws are important to address because they affect network infrastructure equipment.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses HPE Aruba networking equipment, your IT team should handle these updates.
action_it: Apply the latest security updates released by HPE for ArubaOS to address the 72 patched vulnerabilities.

title: Brotli Decoder Flaw Behind Node.js RCE Also Affects Bun, Python and Other Widely Used Software
summary: A security flaw in a widely used data compression tool affects several popular programming tools and software. If exploited, attackers could potentially run malicious code on affected systems.
action_everyone: Most people do not need to do anything. If you use these software tools for development or IT, check for updates from your software providers.
action_it: Identify systems using vulnerable Brotli packages, Bun, or Envoy proxies, and apply software updates as soon as vendors release patches for CVE-2026-111497.

title: BlackX UEFI Bootkit Bypasses Secure Boot on Patched Windows Systems Missing Revocations
summary: A sophisticated bootkit called BlackX has targeted diplomatic organizations in Central Asia by bypassing secure boot protections. This attack highlights sophisticated state-sponsored cyber espionage aimed at government entities.
action_everyone: Most people do not need to do anything, as this attack specifically targeted diplomatic organizations in Central Asia.

title: Quest Diagnostics confirms data breach exposed patient records
summary: Quest Diagnostics disclosed a data breach after an unauthorized person accessed patient records in its Quanum LSM system. This matters because sensitive health and personal information belonging to patients was exposed.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you are a Quest Diagnostics patient, keep an eye on your credit reports and medical statements for unusual activity.
action_it: Investigate unauthorized access within the Quanum LSM system, review access logs, and follow standard incident response procedures for patient data exposure.

title: PHP Warns of Another Unpatched RCE Risk Two Days After Emergency PHP2Shell Patches
summary: PHP disclosed a second security flaw that could let attackers run harmful code on web servers, shortly after patching a previous critical bug. The PHP team is not releasing an emergency patch because the issue only affects unusual setups and requires a specific configuration.

also_covered.title: PHP shares mitigation for new RCE vulnerability with no patch
Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you run a personal website using PHP, check with your web host or IT administrator to ensure your server is configured safely.
action_it: Review server configurations and follow the mitigation advice provided by the PHP security team to disable the affected feature, as no patch is currently planned.

title: Hackers Breach Enterprise Firewalls and VPNs, Exposing Over 70,000 Credentials
summary: Hackers have broken into corporate security gateways like Fortinet and Palo Alto Networks devices, stealing over 70,000 login credentials. This exposes organizations worldwide to further unauthorized access and attacks.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses these network devices, your IT team should investigate for signs of compromise.
action_it: Review access logs on exposed network edge devices for signs of unauthorized activity and ensure all devices are properly secured and monitored.

title: Researchers Push Over 2 Million Updates to Remotely Disable Popcorn Time Updater That Could Fuel a Botnet
summary: Security researchers secretly updated an abandoned pirated video streaming app on over two million computers to disable a feature. This action prevented hackers from potentially taking control of those devices.

also_covered.title: Abandoned Popcorn Time app exposed millions of devices to RCE attacks

title: Exposed Infrastructure Reveals How Ransomware Affiliates Used AI Agents to Execute Intrusions
summary: Cybersecurity researchers discovered that ransomware groups are using an AI-driven system called Phantom to automate network intrusions and data extortion. This matters because the use of artificial intelligence can make cyberattacks faster, harder to detect, and more widespread.

title: Google Says Gmail and Photos Data Shared With AI Search Could Be Used for Targeted Ads
summary: Google updated its privacy policy to state that data from services like Gmail and Photos used in AI search features could be utilized for targeted advertising. This matters because it gives users clearer insight into how their personal information and interactions with artificial intelligence may be tracked across different Google tools for marketing purposes.

title: Microsoft Teams to get AI-powered, context-aware phishing detection
summary: Microsoft is planning to add artificial intelligence to Teams to detect phishing scams starting in November 2026. This will help protect users from malicious links and messages sent through the chat app.

title: Microsoft: Windows Server 2016 reaches end of support in January
summary: Microsoft announced that Windows Server 2016 will stop receiving security updates in January 2027. This matters because running software without security updates leaves systems vulnerable to new cyber attacks.

title: You gave your AI agent access, but who is giving it orders?
summary: Security researchers warn that artificial intelligence assistants can be tricked by malicious emails and websites into performing dangerous actions using their permitted access. This matters because compromised AI agents could steal personal data or delete files on behalf of users without their knowledge.
